fields.TOPIC: Communication of the conformity assessment bodies
fields.CONTENT: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the names and addresses of the designated conformity assessment bodies (CABs); the Commission shall make that information available to all Member States.
fields.PURPOSE: Only bodies that are known can be recognised across borders.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 12a(6) eIDAS · Communication of the assessment bodies Requires the Member States to communicate to the Commission the names and addresses of the conformity assessment bodies they have designated. The parallel provisions are found in Article 5c(7), Article 20(1b) and Article 30(2). Article 20(1b) eIDAS · Notification of the conformity assessment bodies Requires the Member States to notify the Commission without undue delay of the names, addresses AND ACCREDITATION details of the conformity assessment bodies, as well as of any changes thereto; the Commission makes that information available to all Member States. The fact that accreditation details are also subject to notification was added by eIDAS 2.0. Article 30(2) eIDAS · Notification of the designated bodies Requires the Member States to communicate to the Commission the names and addresses of the public or private bodies designated for the certification of qualified electronic signature creation devices; the Commission makes that information available to all Member States.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the certifying body included in the list that has been communicated?
fields.KEY POINT: The same notification mechanism appears in 12a(6), 20(1b) and 30(2).

fields.TOPIC: Delegated act on criteria for conformity assessment bodies
fields.CONTENT: The Commission shall be empowered to adopt DELEGATED acts in accordance with Article 47 establishing specific criteria to be met by the designated conformity assessment bodies (CABs).
fields.PURPOSE: Caution: this is a delegated act (Article 47), not an implementing act (Article 48) – a different procedure and a different right of veto.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 30(4) eIDAS · Delegated act on the designated bodies Empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 47 establishing specific criteria to be met by the designated bodies – the same construction as in Article 5c(8) for the conformity assessment bodies for Wallets. Article 47 eIDAS · Exercise of the delegation Governs the procedure for delegated acts: the duration of the delegation, revocation at any time by the Parliament or the Council, the consultation of experts and the period for objection within which the Parliament or the Council may raise objections. The Regulation refers to Article 47 in only three places: Article 5c(8), Article 24(4b) and Article 30(4).
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Does paragraph 8 empower a delegated act or an implementing act – and which Article governs that procedure?
fields.KEY POINT: 47 = delegated, 48 = implementing. Paragraph 8 takes the 47 route.

fields.TOPIC: Notification of certified and withdrawn European Digital Identity Wallets
fields.CONTENT: Member States shall inform the Commission AND the Cooperation Group WITHOUT UNDUE DELAY of certified European Digital Identity Wallets and of any CANCELLATION of a certification, stating the reasons.
fields.PURPOSE: The revocation must become public just as quickly as the authorisation – otherwise relying parties will continue to rely on a withdrawn Wallet.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5c(1) · Subject matter of certification Defines exhaustively what is certified: the conformity of the Wallet AND of the electronic identification scheme with Article 5a(4), (5) and (8), with the requirement for logical separation under paragraph 14 and, where applicable, with the standards under paragraph 24. Everything else in Article 5a is subject to supervision under Article 46a, not to certification. The number sequence 4-5-8-14 is the practical mnemonic anchor. Article 5e(4) · Publication of the amendment to the list Requires the Commission to publish the corresponding amendments to the list referred to in Article 5d in the Official Journal of the European Union without undue delay. Delayed publication would itself be a security problem, because relying parties would continue to rely on a suspended Wallet. Article 46e eIDAS · European Digital Identity Cooperation Group Establishes the Cooperation Group in which the Member States coordinate practical application. It facilitates peer review and the exchange of experience and issues opinions and recommendations – inter alia on the draft national Wallet certification schemes under Article 5c(3) and on the notifications under Article 5d.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the withdrawal notified as well – or only the initial certification?

fields.CONTENT: The notification shall include at least (a) the certificate and certification assessment report, (b) a description of the electronic identification scheme, (c) the applicable supervisory regime and the LIABILITY REGIME, (d) the responsible authority or authorities, (e) arrangements for suspension or revocation.
fields.PURPOSE: Almost identical in wording to Article 9(1) (notification of electronic identification schemes) – the Wallet follows the same transparency logic.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 9(1) eIDAS · Content of the notification Seven items, points (a) to (g), including the description of the scheme with its assurance levels, the supervisory regime together with the liability regime, set out separately for the issuer and the operator of the authentication procedure, the responsible authorities, the entity managing the registration of the person identification data (PID) and the arrangements for suspension and revocation. Almost congruent with Article 5d(2) for Wallets – the same notification logic in two regimes. Article 5a(19) · Liability reference Provides that Article 11 shall apply mutatis mutandis – without prejudice to paragraph 22. The Wallet therefore follows the liability regime of electronic identification and not that of trust services under Article 13.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Are all five items present, in particular the liability regime under point (c)?
fields.KEY POINT: 5d(2) is the twin of 9(1). Learn it once, know it twice.

fields.TOPIC: List of certified European Digital Identity Wallets
fields.CONTENT: The Commission shall establish, publish in the OFFICIAL JOURNAL and maintain in a MACHINE-READABLE form a list of the certified European Digital Identity Wallets.
fields.PURPOSE: A central, official reference – the counterpart to the trusted list under Article 22.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 9(2) eIDAS · Publication of the list of schemes Requires the Commission to publish the list of notified electronic identification schemes in the Official Journal of the European Union without undue delay. Only that publication triggers the obligation of recognition under Article 6. Article 22 eIDAS · Trusted lists Requires each Member State to establish, maintain and publish lists of the qualified trust service providers and of the qualified trust services provided by them – in a secured manner, electronically signed or sealed and in a form suitable for automated processing. The information on the body responsible for the list, the place of publication and the signature certificates is to be notified to the Commission without undue delay, and the Commission in turn makes it available in a secured manner and in a form suitable for automated processing.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the Wallet included in the list published in the Official Journal?
fields.KEY POINT: EUDI Wallets -> list under 5d. Qualified trust services -> Article 22. Two lists.

fields.CONTENT: Paragraph 4: a Member State MAY submit a request for removal. Paragraph 5: where there are changes, the Member State shall provide updated information. Paragraph 6: the Commission shall publish the amendments WITHIN ONE MONTH of receipt of the request or of the updated information.
fields.PURPOSE: Sets a hard processing deadline to prevent the list from becoming outdated.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 9(3) eIDAS · One-month deadline for amendments Requires the Commission to publish amendments to the notified information in the Official Journal of the European Union within one month of receipt of the notification. The same one-month deadline applies under Article 5d(6) to Wallets and under Article 31(1) to electronic signature creation devices.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Were the amendments notified and published within the deadline?
fields.KEY POINT: One month – the same deadline as for electronic identification schemes under Article 9.

fields.TOPIC: Implementing act on formats and procedures
fields.CONTENT: Implementing act on the formats and procedures for the purposes of paragraphs 1, 4 and 5, within the framework of the implementing act on European Digital Identity Wallets under Article 5a(23).
fields.PURPOSE: Notifications must be capable of automated processing, otherwise the procedure does not scale.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(23) · Implementing act on the core Wallet requirements for Wallets The most important empowering provision of the Regulation in practice. The Commission establishes reference standards, specifications and procedures for paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 – this is the legal basis of the Architecture and Reference Framework. It is at the same time one of the two triggers of the 24-month deadline in paragraph 1. Numerous other provisions (5b(11), 5d(7), 5e(5), 45d(5), 45e(2), 45f(6) and (7)) expressly require alignment with that act. “the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, establish a list of reference standards and, where necessary, establish specifications and procedures for the requirements referred to in paragraphs 4, 5, 8 and 18 of this Article” ✓ Article 5a(23) eIDAS
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Has the implementing act been adopted?

fields.TOPIC: Immediate suspension in the event of compromise
fields.CONTENT: Where the European Digital Identity Wallet, the validation mechanisms referred to in Article 5a(8) or the underlying electronic identification scheme are breached or partly compromised in a manner that affects reliability, the Member State SHALL SUSPEND the provision AND the use WITHOUT UNDUE DELAY. Where justified by the severity, it SHALL WITHDRAW the Wallets without undue delay. The following are to be informed: the users affected, the single points of contact under Article 46c, the relying parties and the Commission.
fields.PURPOSE: A compromised Wallet immediately endangers the entire EU-wide network of trust – a standstill is the lesser evil here.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 5a(6) · Informing users of security breaches Requires the Member State to inform users without delay of any security breach that could have entirely or partially compromised their Wallet or its contents – in particular where it has been suspended or revoked pursuant to Article 5e. The obligation is owed to the user and must be distinguished from notification to the authorities. Article 5a(8) · Free-of-charge validation mechanisms Requires the Member State to provide two free-of-charge verification paths running in opposite directions: point (a) allows verification that a presented Wallet is authentic and valid; point (b) allows the user to verify that the requesting relying party is registered and authentic. Without this two-way verifiability, Article 5b(8) (self-identification of the relying party) could not be verified. It forms part of the subject matter of certification under Article 5c(1). Article 46c eIDAS · Single points of contact Requires each Member State to designate, publish and notify to the Commission a single point of contact for trust services, Wallets and notified electronic identification schemes. Cross-border supervision needs a defined contact point; the single point of contact is, inter alia, an addressee of the notifications under Article 5e. Relevance here: the single point of contact is one of the four mandatory addressees of the notification. Article 10 eIDAS · Security breach of electronic identification schemes Requires the notifying Member State, where a compromise affects reliability, to suspend or revoke the cross-border authentication without delay and to inform the other Member States and the Commission. Once the breach is remedied, cross-border authentication is to be re-established; if it is not remedied for three months, the withdrawal of the scheme is to be notified. The parallel provision for Wallets is Article 5e.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is there a tested emergency process covering all four groups of addressees?
fields.KEY POINT: Four addressees: user, single point of contact, relying party, Commission.

fields.CONTENT: If the security breach is not remedied within THREE MONTHS of the suspension, the Member State SHALL WITHDRAW the European Digital Identity Wallets and SHALL REVOKE their validity; the same four groups of addressees are to be informed again.
fields.PURPOSE: Sets a hard upper limit on states of limbo.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 10(3) eIDAS · Withdrawal of the electronic identification scheme after three months The mirror image of Article 5e(2). If, after suspension or revocation, the breach is not remedied within three months, the notifying Member State notifies the withdrawal of the scheme; the Commission publishes the amendment in the Official Journal of the European Union without undue delay. “three months of the suspension or revocation, the notifying Member State shall notify other Member States and the Commission of the withdrawal of the electronic identification scheme” ✓ Article 10(3) eIDAS Relevance here: an identical three-month deadline – the Wallet and a notified electronic identification scheme are treated with equal strictness. Article 12a(3) eIDAS · Five years, two years, three months A more precise variant of the 5/2 rule: the certification of an electronic identification scheme is valid for up to five years provided that a vulnerability assessment is carried out every two years; where a vulnerability is not remedied within three months of its identification, the certification is to be cancelled. At the same point Article 5c(4) says only 'in a timely manner', and Article 30(3a) gives no deadline at all – a popular exam topic. Article 5a(9) · Grounds for revocation Names three circumstances in which it must be possible to revoke the validity of the Wallet: the explicit request of the user, the compromise of its security, and the death of the user or the cease of activity of the legal person. Article 3 eIDAS · Definitions Contains the legal definitions in points (1) to (57), supplemented by the letter-suffixed points inserted by eIDAS 2.0, such as (5a), (16a) and (21a). Particularly important in practice: point (3) person identification data, point (5a) user, point (6) relying party, point (16) trust service, point (20) qualified trust service provider, point (44) electronic attestation of attributes, point (46) electronic attestation of attributes issued by or on behalf of a public sector body responsible for an authentic source and point (47) authentic source.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the 3-month deadline monitored and documented?
fields.KEY POINT: THREE months, not six – the same limit as Article 10(3).
